rich_narrative.summary: Founded in 1993, Rahima International Foundation is a California-based organization focused on <cite id="1">feeding the hungry and supporting students</cite> in their educational journey. The foundation operates at a significant scale for a regional charity, reporting <cite id="2">$4,006,022 in total revenue in FY2024</cite>. Its primary activities include <cite id="3">food distribution, soup kitchens, and meat collection</cite> for underserved populations in Santa Clara and Alameda counties. While the organization demonstrates a high <cite id="4">program expense ratio of 95.3%</cite> in its financial filings, this figure is tempered by significant governance and capital management concerns. Specifically, the charity maintains <cite id="5">65.0 months of working capital</cite> in working capital, which is more than five years of reserves. This excessive accumulation of funds raises questions about the urgency of aid deployment, especially for an organization that <cite id="6">accepts zakat donations</cite> intended for immediate relief. Furthermore, the organization operates with a <cite id="7">board of only two members</cite>, which falls below standard governance benchmarks for oversight and independent leadership.
